1276:
A. No representation by any official or employee of the city shall in any way legally bind the city or constitute any determination that the building(s) or use(s) located on or proposed for the property involved complies with the city zoning ordinance, or any appendix thereto, in the absence of a certificate of zoning compliance. No owner of property within the city or his or her agent, successor or assign shall be entitled to rely upon any such representation or claim any vested right to build or maintain any building or structure or conduct any use located on or proposed for the property as a result of any such representation.
B. The owner of the property or his or her agent may apply for a certificate of zoning compliance from the building official to determine in advance whether a building, structure or use existing or proposed for any property located within the city is being used or may be used or developed in compliance with this chapter.
C. Such applications shall be in writing on a form provided by the city requiring the following information regarding the property for which a certificate is being requested:
1. Identity of the owner of the property;
2. Identity of any agent of the owner of the property;
3. Property address and Property Identification Number;
4. A complete description and inventory of all existing buildings and structures on the property; (tier 2, only)
5. A complete description and inventory of all proposed buildings and structures to be located on the property; (tier 2, only)
6. A complete description and inventory of all uses established on the property; (tier 2, only)
7. A complete description and inventory of all uses to be established on the property; (tier 2, only) and
8. An ALTA survey of the property representing the current condition. (tier 2, only)
D. The building official shall provide a zoning certificate to the owner within ten business days of receipt of an application for a certificate. Certification of the zoning of the property, the future land use map designation and the zoning designations of abutting properties shall comprise a tier 1 certificate. Certification of compliance of the building(s), use(s) and site shall comprise a tier 2 certificate. Applications for zoning certificates will be processed within ten business days of receipt of a complete application and payment of the appropriate fee.
E. Issuance of a tier 2 zoning certificate shall merely constitute confirmation that the buildings, structures and uses located on or proposed for the property have been determined to be in compliance with the zoning ordinance of the city effective on the date of issuance of the certificate and may be legally conducted thereon as of the date of issuance of the certificate.
(Ord. No. 1166, § 1(Exh. A), 4-5-22)
1277:
A. Certificates of occupancy shall be issued by the building official. No certificate of occupancy shall be issued unless the lot, use and building comply with all provisions of this chapter. A CO must be issued by the building official prior to any occupancy of a building or use of a lot and shall be required under the following circumstances:
1. Initial use of any lot or expansion of an existing use of a lot;
2. A change in the use of an existing building or buildings on the lot or a change in use of the lot;
3. A building has been erected, moved onto the lot, or altered in any manner that required a building permit; or
4. Any nonconforming lot, building or use existing as of the effective date of this chapter or amendment thereto that is changed to a conforming lot, building or use.
B. The building official shall maintain a record of all CO's. A copy of a certificate shall upon receipt of a written request be furnished to any person having a proprietary or tenancy interest in the building or lot involved.
C. The building official shall upon receipt of an application for a certificate of occupancy assess the building and the proposed use and make a determination as to compliance with all applicable zoning; building; traffic and life safety codes, standards, and regulations in cooperation with the Thomaston fire chief and Thomaston police chief. The building official shall also assess compliance of the construction or alteration with the plans submitted with the building permit application and approved by the building official. The building official shall issue a certificate of occupancy to the applicant upon a determination that these requirements have been met. The CO shall clearly identify the use being permitted, any limitations imposed on the use, and a description of any portion of a building or land not to be so used. The building official shall decline to issue a CO for any building, lot or portion thereof upon a determination that these requirements have not been met and shall notify the applicant in writing via hand delivery or certified mail return receipt requested of the denial of the certificate stating the reasons for such denial. Such notice shall be deemed to have been given a minimum of three business days following such mailing.
D. The building official may exclude single family and two family dwellings from the requirement to obtain a certificate of occupancy and may deem final inspection to be final approval.
(Ord. No. 1166, § 1(Exh. A), 4-5-22)
